newsitem.title: UK: Panamaxes still firm in some areas but BFI down.
newsitem.headline: Panamaxes still firm in some areas but BFI down.

text.p: The influence of the forthcoming holidays and continuing loading problems in the Mississippi have been apparent in the freight market.

Brokers said although firm conditions persist for panamaxes in the east and in the South Atlantic the marginal softening of rates elsewhere and the mixed rates obtainable for capers generally were enough to put the BFI down 2 points to 1524, the first fall recorded since 5th march.
Firm rates for handymaxes persisted in the North and South Atlantic and the Handy index was up 3 to 1107.

GRAIN - Andre's reported fixture of HMM tonnage for 52/54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for June at $24.75 no combo could not be confirmed, nor Hanjin's rumoured timecharter fixture of a panamax US Gulf/Far East for first half April.

Brokers said that continuing difficulties in the Mississippi were stifling chartering activity and reducing the level of enquiry. But Cargill booked Lika 118,733 dwt delivery retro sailing Continent 12 March for Mississippi/Holland grain at $9,000 daily, and Dreyfus were said to be looking at caper tonnage for similar business, possibly Commander 123,180 dwt or Eden 138,102 dwt.

Saroc were said to have booked a modern polish bulker of 34,000 dwt delivery US Gulf early April trip Italy at $8,750 daily. Cereol were linked with Sonic Youth 61,569 dwt for grains from the Plate and Rio Grande to various Med options, some claiming that the rate quoted to about $20.75 basis discharging 2 ports Spain.
Arosa 30,499 dwt was fixed on subjects from the Plate to the Med for prompt loading, and Continental were rumoured to have taken Golden Condor 43,214 dwt in this trade, but full details were lacking.

New business quoted today included continental upto panamax size prompt/6 April from the Plate to Red Sea/Arabian Gulf and Toepfer 1/1.4m cft US Gulf/ Gibraltar-Hamburg range including Ireland for 5/15 April.

MINERALS - Brokers reported a higher level of chartering enquiry in the Atlantic. Cetragpa fixed a caper for coal from Maracaibo (38' fw) to Dunkirk east option Fos for 1/10 April at $10.25 and Yukong booked Orfeas 120,144 dwt on subjects La Cienaga/Rotterdam for 5/15 April at $5.90. Vakis T 130,370 dwt was fixed by Pan Ocean delivery prompt Lisbon for 4-6 months at $8,750 daily but failed on subjects and these charterers were believed to have fixed United Respect (ex Baron Bay) 149,212 dwt delivery Rotterdam mid April for a trip via Richards Bay to s korea at d14,750 daily, also on subjects. Elsewhere there were rumours P and O had fixed Docebay 152,308 dwt for Richards Bay coal to Denmark and that Eridge 122,792 dwt had been fixed from Kaohsiung for a trip via Australia to Japan on private terms.
A number of period fixtures of modern panamaxes were concluded in the east, and Australian rounds were booked at between $13,000 and $13,500 daily for the most economical types.

The newbuilding Wintrader went to Navix delivery ex yard Japan March/April for a silica sand round via Queensland at $13,500 daily. Alkimos 41,416 dwt was fixed delivery Arabian Gulf via S.Africa to the Baltic, and Akmi 26,874 dwt went to Alcan for alumina from La Plata.
